# SMALL PLEOMORPHIC BACILLI IN AEROBIC BOTTLE

Small pleomorphic bacilli in aerobic bottle are usually diphtheroids. These are usually contaminants. Uncommonly such organisms prove to be Listeria monocytogenes, which when present in a blood culture is likely a pathogen.

Listeria is more likely in patients with impaired cell-mediated immunity, pregnant women, elderly and patients on immunosuppressive therapy for transplantation.

References

- Mandell chapter: Listeria Monocytogenes
- Mandell chapter: Other Coryneform Bacteria and Rhodococci
- Medical Letter Choice of Antimicrobials 2010, 8.94
- Sanford keyword: Listeria monocytogenes
- Sanford keyword: Propionibacterium acnes
- Sanford keyword: Corynebacterium
Therapy:
## Empirical treatment if there is a strong suspicion of listeria

[Ampicillin 2 gm IV q4h \(Cost $$\) R](psjizid-ampicillin-2-gm-iv-q4h)

For immunocompromised, meningitis or endocarditis
[Ampicillin 2 gm IV q4h \(Cost $$\) R and gentamicin 1.7 mg/kg IV q8h \(Cost](orz-set-abx-ampicil-2g-q4h-gent-1-7mg-kg-iv-q8h)
$) [R,O]

For patients with penicillin allergy
[Trimethoprim 5 mg/kg - sulfamethoxazole 25 mg/kg IV q12h \(Cost $$$\) R,DI](psjizid-trimethoprim-sulfameth-5-25-mg-kg-iv-q12h)

## Empirical treatment if therapy is indicated and listeria is not suspected

[Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h \(Cost $\) R](orz-set-abx-vanco-new-start-15mg-kg-q12h-mrsa-nares-screening)
